alerts.title: Abdominal pain requires ADR screening and reporting
alerts.message: Guidelines require all health workers to screen every patient encounter for suspected adverse drug reactions using the Drug Safety Screening checklist, and all suspected ADRs, whether mild or severe, must be recorded in ART cards, registers, and eMRS and reported. The patient reports abdominal pain with no fever and preserved appetite while on TDF/3TC/DTG since March 2023. The symptom checklist includes abdominal complaints among adverse events to be assessed at each visit. No cause has been documented, and no ADR screening or reporting action appears in today's plan.

evidence.recommended_action: Complete the Drug Safety Screening checklist for abdominal pain, record findings in the ART card and eMRS, and submit a suspected ADR report if drug causation is suspected.

alerts.title: Abdominal pain on TDF warrants clinical evaluation
alerts.message: Guideline toxicity references list abdominal pain among adverse events associated with ART drugs, including upper abdominal pain with hepatotoxicity presentations. The patient has been on TDF/3TC/DTG for nearly three years and now reports abdominal pain without fever. TDF can cause renal tubular dysfunction and hepatotoxicity, though her creatinine of 82 umol/L 78 days ago is normal, which argues against significant TDF nephrotoxicity. Non-drug causes such as gastritis, infection, or other gastrointestinal pathology should also be considered. The clinician's plan documents the symptom but contains no evaluation, differential diagnosis, or monitoring orders.

evidence.recommended_action: Evaluate the abdominal pain clinically, consider TDF-related hepatotoxicity or renal effects, and investigate non-drug causes; repeat creatinine and liver function tests if indicated.

alerts.title: Clinician plan lacks action for reported symptom
alerts.message: The clinician's assessment and plan today only restates the patient's complaint of abdominal pain without any diagnostic workup, treatment, monitoring orders, or follow-up instructions. Guidelines require that every encounter includes active screening for suspected adverse drug reactions and that identified symptoms are acted upon and documented. The patient's viral load of 25 copies/mL confirms virological suppression, so regimen failure is unlikely to explain the symptom. The absence of any planned action for a new symptom in a stable patient represents a care gap that should be addressed at this visit.

evidence.recommended_action: Document a differential diagnosis and management plan for the abdominal pain, including any indicated investigations, symptom-directed treatment, and a defined follow-up interval.
